title: Amber Specimen Analysis Lab
description: The user operates a forensic light analysis station where an iridescent lamp illuminates a mosquito preserved in amber. By adjusting post-processing effect chains—bloom, chromatic aberration, tone mapping, vignette, and color grading—the user reveals hidden spectral layers within the amber specimen. A conservation law ensures total luminance energy is preserved across all effects, and full undo/redo history tracks every adjustment.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with postprocessing via EffectComposer from three/addons. Load IridescenceLamp.glb positioned at (-2, 0, 0) aimed toward center, and MosquitoInAmber.glb at (0, 0, 0) on a dark pedestal. Camera at (0, 2, 5) with OrbitControls. Use a dim ambient light plus a point light parented to the lamp model. Build an EffectComposer chain with these passes: RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, ShaderPass for chromatic aberration, ShaderPass for vignette, ShaderPass for color grading (RGB lift/gamma/gain), and an OutputPass with tone mapping exposure control. Create a dat.gui panel with sliders: bloom strength (0-3), bloom radius (0-1), bloom threshold (0-1), chromatic aberration offset (0-0.02), vignette darkness (0-2), vignette offset (0-2), RGB gain per channel (0-2 each), and tone mapping exposure (0-3). Implement a conservation law: total luminance energy equals bloom_strength + exposure + average_RGB_gain and must always equal a constant value of 4.0. When the user increases one parameter, the others auto-scale proportionally downward to maintain the sum. Display the current energy budget as a HUD bar. Implement an undo/redo system: every slider change pushes a snapshot of all parameter values onto a history stack. Bind Cmd+Z for undo and Cmd+Shift+Z for redo, restoring all sliders and effect parameters simultaneously. Add a toggle button that switches between normal view and a false-color spectral view using a custom ShaderPass that maps luminance to a rainbow gradient. The lamp model should slowly rotate its iridescent shade, causing the point light color to cycle through hues over 10 seconds, dynamically affecting all post-processing results. Show step counter tracking total interactions performed.
